bullets.title: Iran/Middle East escalation spikes crude, drives early tape pressure
bullets.body: US-Iran tensions dominated Monday's open: Iran TV declared Hormuz would stay closed until US ends interference, explosions were heard near Bandar Abbas and Qeshm Island, and Bahrain confirmed intercepting multiple Iranian aerial attacks. Brent crude surged ~4% to above $79/bbl, WTI +3.5% to ~$73.89, UK 10-year gilts broke above 4.90% on the oil move, and S&P futures were down ~0.3-0.4% early before recovering to roughly flat (+0.3% per StreetAccount).

bullets.title: KOSPI circuit-breaker panic and SK Hynix -15% ripple through memory/semis
bullets.body: South Korean stocks fell 9% overnight, bringing the KOSPI's year-to-date circuit-breaker halts to 7 (13 total this century) and the index's drawdown from peak to 25.3%. SK Hynix plunged a record 15%, dragging US memory proxies: SNDK -5.6%, MU -5.3%, WDC -5.1% in premarket. The move was characterized broadly as 'sell the news' on the SK Hynix ADR debut rather than a fundamental negative, with the SK Hynix CEO reiterating memory shortage expectations beyond 2030 and clients wanting 5-6x capacity.

bullets.title: MS QDS flags record-low implied correlations and VIX spike risk into CPI/FOMC
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley QDS warns that S&P 500 implied correlations have collapsed to 7% — an all-time low — while single-stock volatility sits at crisis-period highs. If correlations mean-revert while single-name vol stays elevated, index vol has significant room to rise; dealer short-vega positioning would amplify any spike. CPI is priced for only 51bps SPX move and FOMC for 79bps, both seen as underpriced. SPX 1-month downside skew is in the 20th percentile vs. the past year, and correlation skew in the 19th percentile since 2020.

bullets.title: JPM tilts bullish on Tuesday's CPI: 70% probability of 25-125bp SPX gain on in-line print
bullets.body: JPM's Michael Feroli forecasts Headline CPI -0.20% MoM (3.7% YoY) and Core +0.22% MoM (2.8% YoY). JPM Market Intelligence assigns 70% probability to a Core print of 0.15-0.30%, which would generate 25-125bp SPX gains; only a 5% chance Core exceeds 0.30% (100-200bp decline). Options are pricing ~70bps move vs. historical 100-110bps, suggesting micro/earnings now dominates over macro. A dovish print would steepen the yield curve, supporting Cyclicals and acting as a Tech tailwind.

bullets.title: Hyperscaler capex raised to $1.2T in '27 / $1.4T in '28; META top pick across multiple banks
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley's Brian Nowak raised estimates ~10% vs. prior: META capex $225B/'27 and $250B/'28, AMZN $308B/'27 and $318B/'28, GOOGL $350B/'27 and $375B/'28, with total AI data center compute reaching 120GW by 2028 (4x from 2025). META separately confirmed a $50B+ expansion of its Richland Parish, Louisiana campus to 5GW, bringing total project cost toward $250B. Cost per GW is up ~20% due to memory and powered shell inflation; data center build timelines have stretched to 3 years. META remains MS's top internet pick.

bullets.title: TSMC June revenue +67.9% YoY to $13.8B; Q2 record $39.6B; 1.4nm on track for Q3 2027 pilot
bullets.body: TSMC reported June 2026 revenue of $13.8B (+67.9% YoY, +6.2% MoM), capping a record Q2 at $39.63B (+36% YoY). Analysts expect management to lift full-year guidance from 'above 30%' to 'at least 35%'. Separately, TSMC's 1.4nm process is encountering zero roadblocks with first fab nearing completion and pilot production targeted for Q3 2027. JPM forecasts server CPU TAM reaching ~$100B by 2028 at 53% CAGR, with agentic-AI CPUs ramping at 155% CAGR — a broad tailwind for the TSMC supply chain.

bullets.title: Morgan Stanley CIO Wilson: broadening earnings recovery; 2Q EPS +19% YoY, AI realization at 25% of S&P 500
bullets.body: MS CIO Mike Wilson notes the median S&P 1500 company is delivering double-digit EPS growth (strongest since post-COVID), with equal-weighted S&P 500 outperforming cap-weighted since mid-May. 2Q EPS is expected at +19% YoY / sales +9% YoY. 40% of AI-adopter companies cited measurable AI benefits in 2Q26 (up from 21% a year ago), and ~25% of all S&P 500 companies reported tangible AI gains (from 14%). Technology leads AI realization at 51% of companies.

bullets.title: US equity positioning at 6-month bullish extremes; SPX dealer gamma at 99th percentile
bullets.body: US equity consensus has returned to its most bullish readings in 6 months per Hedgeye, and Jefferies notes SPX dealer gamma is at the 99th percentile, suppressing volatility within a 7200-7650 range. GS reports AI/momentum de-grossing occurred recently, with $56.4B flowing into equities last week ($18.8B into Tech). GS High Momentum gross exposure is at the 90th percentile (down from the 99th on June 22). 22V notes single-name volatility trades at a record premium to index vol, making VIX hedges structurally attractive.

bullets.title: Power costs surge to 17-year highs on data-center demand; oil/energy names lead gains
bullets.body: Natural gas power costs hit $90/MWh in 2026 — the highest in at least 17 years — with solar and onshore wind costs also up 10%+, driven by accelerating data-center demand. Energy/oil sector stocks are broadly outperforming on the Iran escalation; Canadian energy names (EOG.CN +3.4%, HWX.CN +3.3%) led the TSX. The US Strategic Petroleum Reserve has fallen to its lowest level since 1983, limiting a policy buffer.

bullets.title: Goldman warns chip-supplier multiples at risk if hyperscaler capex draws investor pushback
bullets.body: Goldman cautioned that even if chip-supplier earnings grow, hardware names could face multiple compression if hyperscalers come under investor pressure to cut capex. This is the central bear case for the AI infrastructure trade, distinct from a demand slowdown — and is separate from the near-term SK Hynix/memory unwind.

bullets.title: Semis breadth rotation: Wolfe bullish AVGO/NVDA at discount; AMAT top SCE name; QCOM still a show-me story
bullets.body: Wolfe Research's chip webcast sees AVGO and NVDA both trading at a discount and recommends owning both to hedge single-name risk. AVGO management is highly optimistic its 20GW XPV financing vehicle closes, leaving ~14GW of incremental OpenAI/Anthropic capacity for FY28. Semi-cap base case is $225B CY28 WFE (up to $265B bear/bull). AMAT is the preferred SCE long on valuation and DRAM exposure. QCOM remains a show-me story; street is missing the full $5B FY27 datacenter guidance. MU remains bullish post-pullback, with customer supply commitment agreements providing multi-year visibility.

bullets.title: AI infrastructure bottleneck has shifted from chips to physical deployment capacity
bullets.body: A detail from WhiteFiber's Q1 call noted that enterprise customers already hold 2027 GPU purchase orders but lack the building and placement infrastructure to deploy them. This corroborates MS data that data center build timelines have stretched to 3 years and points to a structural opportunity in power, construction, and real estate adjacent to AI compute.

bullets.title: AI data sovereignty becoming enterprise software theme; Karp/Nadella/Benioff echoing same concern
bullets.body: Palantir CEO Alex Karp's AI sovereignty messaging is triggering a preference cascade: Satya Nadella's essay on the 'Reverse Information Paradox' (enterprises pay both money and proprietary data to frontier models) and Salesforce's Benioff are echoing the same concern. MS notes this favors private/tenant-controlled hybrid AI architectures, with enterprises routing routine workloads to cheaper open models while reserving frontier models for complex tasks. Chinese and open-source model adoption rose to 5.8% of AI-spending businesses in June from 4.5% in January.

bullets.title: CPI/macro week: 22V and Piper flag persistent inflation risk; M2 growth too stimulative at 7%
bullets.body: 22V flags CPI and PPI as primary near-term market direction drivers. A separate macro note argues M2 growth of ~7% implies the current 3.63% fed funds rate is still too stimulative, with nominal bond yields of 4.5% consistent with 6% nominal GDP — potentially rising toward 5% if nominal growth sustains. Tech price increases (Apple, Microsoft +20-30%, surging DRAM) are keeping core inflation sticky despite lower headline CPI. Core PCE is elevated at 3.4%.

bullets.title: Asia risk-off contagion: Shanghai -2.1% to 3-month lows; Nikkei -1.9%; Japan/China exits flagged
bullets.body: Beyond Korea, broader Asian equity weakness added to Monday's pressure: Shanghai fell 2.1% to new 3-month lows and the Nikkei dropped 1.9% overnight. These moves were cited as contributing to US futures pressure alongside the Iran developments.

bullets.title: Ukraine hits all 10 major Russian oil refineries; >25% of Russian refining offline
bullets.body: Ukraine has now struck all 10 of Russia's largest oil refineries in 2026, with analyst estimates suggesting more than 25% of Russian refining capacity is offline. This is an incremental supply disruption on top of the Iran/Hormuz headlines, reinforcing the oil bid.

bullets.title: Wolfe Bay Area bus tour positive across SaaS; AI budgets shifting from token volume to token efficiency
bullets.body: Wolfe's channel checks from a Bay Area SaaS tour found SNOW confident in Cortex/CoCo revenue upside, CRM evolving Slack into an AI runtime with TAM-expansion potential, ZM seeing high-double-digit growth post-Voice Agent, and PANW/CRWD both citing strong Mythos-driven pipeline. VC meetings indicate AI budgets are shifting from 'tokenmaxxing' to token efficiency, with total spend not declining but composition changing. Potential for increased strategic M&A in 2H 2026.

bullets.title: PC notebook demand faces 2H headwinds from memory/CPU price increases; full-year -8-12% Y/Y
bullets.body: KeyBanc's June ODM analysis shows June notebook shipments of 16.8M (+23% MoM, -5% YoY) met estimates, driven by pre-pricing-increase pull-ins. However, 2H demand is expected to weaken materially: Q3 at -3% QoQ / -11% YoY, Q4 at -15% QoQ / -14% YoY, with full-year 2026 projected -8-12% YoY as memory and CPU price increases bite.

bullets.title: Warsh Fed-chair expectations broadly positive; 61% of investors see above-average performance
bullets.body: A Bespoke mid-year survey found 61% of investors expect Warsh to perform above-average as Fed Chair, with only 7% expecting below-average results. Rajan argues the Fed should move slowly on balance sheet reduction and monitor bank liability-side management to avoid moral hazard.

bullets.title: Citi downgrades UK equities to Underweight from Overweight; defensive/commodity-heavy composition a drag
bullets.body: Citi cut its UK stock market rating to Underweight from Overweight, citing that while valuations remain attractive, the market's defensive and commodity-heavy composition is ill-suited to the current earnings-growth environment. UK gilts also broke above 4.90% on the oil spike, outpacing advanced-economy peers and adding pressure to UK risk assets.
